correctness.rationale: A complete derivation first computes the conditional gap in \(K_n\) after a tagged coincidence, then uses exchangeability when \(m\le n\), and a two-future-customer exact prediction when \(m>n\). The key \(K_n\) coefficient cancels \(K_n\) from future pair-collision probabilities, producing exact affine projection. All denominators are positive on the stated domain; the empty product \(n=2\), \(\alpha=0\), negative allowed theta, and gamma-ratio limit are checked. An independent exact-Fraction enumeration for four parameter pairs, every 2<=n<=5 and 2<=m<=6, agrees; finite enumeration is only corroboration.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison of Pitman–Yor finite-sample EPPF, Pitman conditional prediction, Cerquetti conditional diversity, a published fixed-iid categorical covariance theorem, and modern hierarchical Pitman–Yor diversity predictions did not find the explicit two-time signed kernel. Crucially, a fixed-p conditional covariance does not imply the unconditional random-frequency covariance, which includes a between-P term. An EPPF defines finite sums but does not evaluate the exact prefix-flat/future-separable form. Search non-detection is not proof; possible older equivalences remain a documented risk.
residual_risks: Earlier population-genetic homozygosity or species-sampling notation may encode the same evaluated covariance without matching current searches.
The general EPPF is sufficiently powerful to imply the identity by finite summation; a yet-unlocated paper might have carried out this specific simplification.

value.rationale: The covariance of sample richness with empirical Simpson concentration is a natural joint functional for diversity analysis. The finding evaluates the complete two-index kernel for all sizes and all two-parameter CRP laws, classifies its strict sign and \(m\le n\) exact invariance, provides a separable kernel for \(m>n\), and exhibits a sharp constant-versus-\(n^\alpha\) scaling distinction. This structure is not a generic one-line recoding of an existing same-time moment.
